about.title: La Mirada Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Falls happen fast, often in a shopping center along Rosecrans Avenue, a grocery store near La Mirada Boulevard, or an apartment complex off Valley View Avenue — and the aftermath can leave you with more questions than answers. La Mirada's mix of retail plazas, restaurants, and residential properties means property owners have a duty to keep walkways, parking lots, and stairwells reasonably safe. Under California law, though, a fall alone isn't enough to build a claim; you generally need to show the property owner or manager knew, or should have known, about the hazard and didn't fix it or warn you. That's why documenting what caused your fall and pushing for surveillance footage before it's erased matters so much. LawProactive doesn't practice law, but we can connect you with an independent attorney who handles these cases and can walk you through what evidence to gather and what deadlines apply to your situation.

whyChoose.title: Why Notice and Evidence Matter in Your Case

items.title: Proving the Owner Knew or Should Have Known
items.desc: California premises law generally requires showing the property owner had notice of the hazard and failed to address it. An attorney can help identify inspection logs, complaint history, or how long a hazard existed.

items.title: Preserving Surveillance Video Before It's Gone
items.desc: Many La Mirada retail centers and apartment properties overwrite security footage within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation of that video can be critical to your claim.

items.title: Understanding Comparative Fault
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning your recovery can be reduced but not eliminated if you're found partly responsible. An attorney can help present your case in a way that accounts for this fairly.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in La Mirada?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury lawsuit. If your fall happened on public property, such as a city sidewalk or a government building, that deadline can be much shorter, sometimes just six months. Speaking with an attorney early helps protect your options.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for my fall?
items.answer: California's pure comparative fault rule means you can still recover damages even if you share some responsibility, though your award may be reduced by your percentage of fault. This is common in busy areas near Imperial Highway or La Mirada Boulevard where lighting, weather, or foot traffic can complicate what happened. An attorney can help sort out how fault might be allocated in your specific case.

items.question: Do I really need surveillance footage to have a case?
items.answer: Video isn't always required, but it can be one of the strongest pieces of evidence showing how long a hazard was present and whether staff had a chance to notice it. Many stores and property managers in La Mirada only retain footage for a limited window, so requesting preservation quickly matters. An independent attorney can help send that request on your behalf.
